title: Shrinking a nodal model chart to make its parameter invertible off a boundary
statement: Let $V$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $h\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, and put $W=\operatorname{Spec}_V(\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h))$, the gluing of these affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $e:U\to W$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], write $p:U\to V$ for its structure map, and fix $t\in U$ such that $e(t)$ belongs to the closed subscheme $N=V(u,v)\subset W$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $T\subset V$ be a closed subset and suppose $p$ is smooth over $V\setminus T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Under the projection isomorphism $N\simeq V(h)$, let $Z$ be the image of $N\setminus e(U)$. Then $Z$ is closed in $V$, $p(t)\notin Z$, and for $V^\circ=V\setminus Z$ and $U^\circ=U\times_VV^\circ$ [def-pc-base-change] every point of $V(h)\cap V^\circ$ has its corresponding node in the image of $U^\circ$. The given point $t$ remains in $U^\circ$, and $h|_{V^\circ\setminus T}$ is invertible. No surjectivity of $e$ on all of $W$, no properness, and no reducedness assumption on $V(h)$ are imposed.

source.place: Exposé VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71, equation (1.a): the function h invertible on Y minus T; explicit neighbourhood shrinking for the Stacks curves.tex Tag 0CBY model.

proof.text: On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$, setting $u=v=0$ gives $(A[u,v]/(uv-h))/(u,v)=A/(h)$. These coefficient-preserving identifications agree under restriction, hence give the projection isomorphism $N\simeq V(h)$ as schemes. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], this projection identifies $|N|$ with a closed subspace of $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], $e(U)$ is open in $W$. Consequently $N\setminus e(U)$ is closed in $N$, and its image $Z$ is closed in $V$. Since $e(t)\in N\cap e(U)$, its image $p(t)$ does not lie in $Z$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71, equation (1.a); explicit closed-complement shrinking for the model of Stacks Tag 0CBY.

proof.text: For $s\in V(h)\cap V^\circ$, let $n_s$ be the unique corresponding point of $N$. The definition of $Z$ implies $n_s\in e(U)$, so choose $r\in U$ with $e(r)=n_s$. Then $p(r)=s\in V^\circ$. Base change to an open subscheme is restriction to its inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]; thus $r$ belongs to $U^\circ=U\times_VV^\circ$ and maps to the corresponding node in $W\times_VV^\circ$. The same argument and $p(t)\notin Z$ show that $t$ remains in $U^\circ$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, equation (1.a): neighbourhood restriction retaining all nodes over the surviving zero locus.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-polynomial-free-flat], $\pi:W\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-model-etale-smooth-locus] with $X=W$, $Y=V$, $f=\pi$, $b=\operatorname{id}_V$, $q=e$, and the given $p$ and $e$. The identities are etale by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $\pi e=p$, so all hypotheses hold. It follows that $p$ is nonsmooth at every $r\in U$ with $e(r)\in N$. If $s\in V(h)\cap(V^\circ\setminus T)$, step 2 supplies such an $r$ above $s$. But $p$ is smooth over the open $V\setminus T$ by hypothesis, hence is smooth at $r$, a contradiction. Therefore $V(h)\cap(V^\circ\setminus T)=\varnothing$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71: h invertible on Y minus T; nonsmooth-model test from morphisms.tex Tag 01V9.

proof.text: Put $O=V^\circ\setminus T$. For any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset O$, write $a=h|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$. Step 3 says that no prime of $A$ contains $a$. If $(a)$ were proper, a maximal ideal containing it would be prime, a contradiction. Hence $ac=1$ for some $c\in A$. The inverse sections so obtained agree on overlaps, since any two inverses of the same element are equal; the structure sheaf glues them to an inverse of $h|_O$. This also covers the empty open. Thus $h|_O$ is invertible, with no hypothesis on nilpotents in $V(h)$.
